prompts.task: Scan the AI assistant FastAPI service in ./service for OpenTelemetry, GenAI readiness, and Splunk Agent Observability deployment gaps. Do not modify service code, dependencies, configuration, or tests. Only the required .observe audit artifacts may be written. Write and validate canonical ./service/.observe/otel-audit.json first, then render self-contained ./service/.observe/otel.html from that JSON.

Produce an observability readiness review for the AI assistant service in ./service. Identify existing telemetry, GenAI pathway gaps, incident-detection impact, and the next instrumentation step. Do not modify service code, dependencies, configuration, or tests. Only the required .observe audit artifacts may be written. Write and validate canonical ./service/.observe/otel-audit.json first, then render self-contained ./service/.observe/otel.html from that JSON.

judge_inputs: Inspect ./service for app.py, eval_runner.py, load_demo.py, pyproject.toml, README.md, canonical .observe/otel-audit.json, and generated HTML output when present.
Read ./last_message.md for the agent final response.
rubric: Identifies app.py, load_demo.py, pyproject.toml, and FastAPI routes for chat, streaming chat, stream inventory, feedback, and feedback export.

Reports that interactive app.py has no custom OpenTelemetry SDK setup, no GenAI semantic-convention spans or metrics, and no runtime exporter/resource binding beyond demo environment variables. Separately recognizes that eval_runner.py already owns supported AO project resolution, a dedicated evaluation Agent Stream, SDK-created trace/model spans, direct export, flush, and matching logger.terminate in finally; does not incorrectly describe the whole repository as having no AO instrumentation.
Maps GenAI readiness gaps for provider/model calls, tool fanout, token/context pressure, streaming lifecycle, prompt/response outcome, and offline AI data export.

Detects the document lookup inside search_docs from its code path; writes a retrieval-specific readiness row and a selectable OTel retrieval finding with its own ID, separate from the tool row and tool finding, plus a verification scenario for one nested gen_ai.operation.name=retrieval span. A combined tool-and-retrieval row or finding does not pass.

Writes schema-v2 .observe/otel-audit.json with GenAI ownership detected as Yes, a matching audit-evidence entry, and GenAI readiness data with one entry per readiness surface and explicit required signals; validates it before rendering HTML.

For both prompts, including genai-readiness without explicit AO wording, completes an independent Splunk AO assessment for the interactive FastAPI runtime and the offline eval_runner.py runtime. Cites process entry points, import/callback/logger registration reachability, and source-backed negative evidence showing evaluation-only configuration is not reachable from live app.py chat. Keeps evaluation AO resource, trace, and teardown ownership source-covered without claiming runtime delivery; never lets that covered evaluation row mask absent interactive project binding, dedicated live stream, or runtime routing. Does not propose unnecessary repair of the already-covered evaluation route or reuse its stream/logger as proof of live chat coverage.

Represents the absent interactive Splunk Agent Observability project binding, dedicated live Agent Stream binding, and runtime routing as separate independently selectable configuration findings with finding_group=splunk-agent-observability in the canonical findings array, each with process-relative evidence and acceptance scenarios. Uses fix all for optional live adoption in the broad genai-readiness prompt when no product target was selected, and default for safe AO project, stream, and route findings when the user explicitly requested AO deployment gaps; absence of audit-time cloud credentials must not downgrade those requested findings to fix all. Does not require arbitrary unrelated non-AO services to adopt the product. The stream depends on the project and runtime routing depends on both plus the OTel export path, so selecting routing can auto-include the distinct prerequisites. Missing audit-time credentials alone do not make the project external follow-up. Ordinary OpenTelemetry findings have no finding_group and no fabricated span or metric represents control-plane work. Selects an available cloud-compatible Splunk Observability Studio gateway as the default local destination, while preserving explicit operator endpoints and direct-cloud mode. Assesses normal SDK/API project and stream calls, supported endpoint/auth configuration, per-request routing, and fresh cloud stream visibility separately; an SDK compatibility gap must be stated exactly. Connecting Studio alone does not provision a project or stream. Local receipt, a resource API response, an upstream ingest acknowledgement, or ordinary APM visibility is not cloud Agent Observability proof. Does not demand application cloud tokens in gateway mode or propose a Studio-specific application adapter, runtime endpoint discovery, or global destination registration. A stopped or disconnected selected gateway is a delivery prerequisite, not a reason to silently replace the operator's destination.

When the fixture has no verifiably running local gateway or live target, names Splunk Observability Studio as the preferred local AO gateway candidate but records availability and concrete endpoint as unverified rather than inventing an address. Classifies the installed SDK's project/stream API endpoint and per-request trace-routing compatibility as supported with source proof, unsupported with the exact contract gap, or unverified with the exact unavailable package/runtime evidence; generic cloud-compatible wording alone is insufficient.

Keeps each live AO routing finding acceptance-complete under selection: its transitive dependency closure includes every missing workflow, agent, model, tool, or retrieval span producer required by that routing finding's accepted trace structure, not merely an exporter or outer workflow. It can omit a producer prerequisite only with source-covered creation reachable from that exact runtime. Selecting only the routing finding must therefore auto-include all promised missing operation producers while leaving unrelated optional telemetry unselected; neither an evaluation trace nor an export-only SDK processor proves live operation creation.

Each new live AO route includes source-backed matching provider or SDK sink teardown in its executable closure and a dedicated credential-free local lifecycle scenario attached to the routing finding or its selected lifecycle prerequisite. Reuses the ordinary OTel provider lifecycle finding when it closes that runtime instead of inventing duplicate AO lifecycle work; eval_runner.py logger.terminate never closes interactive provider.shutdown. A fake-sink or in-memory scenario exercises the live route's force_flush/shutdown or supported logger termination, verifies pending completed spans are drained and resources released, inspects every active application and AO sink, and proves exactly one canonical workflow/model/tool operation with no duplicate producer or duplicate export to the same AO destination. A vague flush or no-duplicates acceptance sentence without this executable scenario is insufficient. Keep optional cloud receipt proof distinct from these credential-free local lifecycle and single-sink checks.

Renders Splunk Agent Observability findings as the only nested subsection under the one Findings section, with ordinary OTel cards directly under Findings rather than under a new OpenTelemetry findings heading. The rendered order keeps every required finding above every recommended finding even when both AO and ordinary OTel cards exist. AO subsection headings label their cards, grouped card detail headings are subordinate to those subsection headings, and ordinary OTel card details retain their direct-under-Findings hierarchy. Selecting a downstream AO finding auto-includes executable prerequisites while preserving explicit intent separately.
Keeps privacy and cardinality safe by not recommending raw prompt, completion, session, user, request, or tool argument values as metric dimensions.

Renders self-contained .observe/otel.html from the validated JSON without making the reader view authoritative, and leaves a selection-aware audit reader that downstream instrumentation or verification rendering can preserve without resetting its selected findings.
